notes: EXACT same architecture family as CodingAgent-20B, scaled to the 3B class. Width halved (6144->3072, 16384->7168, 48/8->24/4), depth 60->20, thinner SwiGLU MLP (intermediate 7168, ratio 2.33x), head_dim 128, RoPE 500k, sliding window 4096, vocab 128256 preserved. See model/config_3b.py for breakdown. Throughput recipe: 4096-token sequences (native 8192 / YaRN 32k / 64k contexts remain available for inference), micro-batch 1 per GPU with a 512 global batch, and ZeRO-3 with everything resident on the GPU (2.55B params: ~5.1 GB of bf16 weights, ~5.1 GB of grads and ~20.4 GB of Adam fp32 state, sharded across ranks). Offload is deliberately OFF: at 3B the optimizer state fits, and streaming it over PCIe every step was the single largest throughput loss in the old recipe. Activation checkpointing uses one segment per block: measured against the estimator it is the setting whose peak is *below* the old configuration, while two segments (the more common default) trades ~0.5 GiB of peak for a few percent of step time. If a rank cannot hold its shard, either add ranks or enable configs/ds_config_zero3_offload.json (same math, ~2 GB/rank instead of ~10 GB). The 3B pretrainer uses its own 18B-token budget; shared data mixture settings are unchanged.

compile.note: torch.compile on the block stack; opt-in because it costs a few minutes of warmup on the first steps.
